checks: Opening the default study does not create or overwrite a recovery record
The actual file picker accepts recovery-still.json
Opening a document restores its working swatches without applying a palette adjustment
A changed workspace swatch is serialized without modifying artwork RGBA or adding a rendering layer
Reload retains the successful previous recovery transaction
Recovery remains an explicit choice and does not silently replace the opening canvas
Restoring a browser record reproduces source RGB, partial and hidden alpha, silhouette, masks, height layers and working palette
The source-selection regression begins with a real captured pointer on the source canvas
Recovery releases the source canvas pointer before editing resumes
Restoring ends and releases an active source-selection gesture so subsequent pointer movement cannot edit the restored document
A reopened tab writes to a new record instead of overwriting its previous recovery source
Deleting a recovery record keeps the current editable drawing and swatches
Restore makes a durable backup of the current drawing even after its own recovery record was deleted
Reload before further editing offers the restored source, while the pre-restore backup remains available
A synchronous second-store failure aborts the transaction and preserves both previous data and summary stores
Explicit save can recover after a failed storage transaction
Explicit save recreates unchanged data after another storage connection deletes its record
Disabling autosave during a pending transaction prevents subsequent edits from being drained into storage
The manual recovery-save button still works when automatic saving is disabled
The actual file picker accepts recovery-animation.json
Animation recovery retains a cel palette including partial alpha and a distinct optional top-level fallback without creating a palette on the other cel
A cel with its own working palette takes precedence over the animation fallback
Per-cel palette selection preserves source RGB, partial and hidden alpha, silhouette, independent height edits and authored frame timing
A cel without a working palette displays the optional animation fallback
Viewing and saving the fallback cel changes only navigation and does not materialize fallback swatches or modify any cel artwork
Returning to the first cel preserves the exact project, both palette scopes and all authored pixels
Reload and recovery reproduce the exact animation with independent cel geometry, frame durations, direction, per-cel swatches and top-level fallback
The actual file picker accepts recovery-palette-256.json
Reopening a valid 256-color palette layer remains saveable with all workspace swatches and the same layer ID
An invalid stored project reports a recoverable error and leaves the current validated artwork intact
Recovery controls and long draft names fit the 390px viewport
Storage failure, reload and restore complete without uncaught errors or rejected promises
